title: SLA drift: bifurcated TTFT regression across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — urgent hotpatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several key customers reported a sudden bifurcated regression in TTFT and sustained tokens/sec drops beginning 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. The behavior manifests differently across deployment modes: Hosted sees high variance with regional spikes, Dedicated shows throughput erosion under mixed-model fanout, and Private clusters report sustained first-token lag for long-context requests. This ticket coordinates a triage, short-term hotpatch, and follow-up engineering work to restore SLOs and prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use model 'o1-large' and 'o1-quant' in a mixed fanout setup with 80/20 traffic split; send 5k concurrent short prompts (avg 20 tokens) to Hosted region us-west-2 over 10 minutes
2) Create Dedicated reservation with 3 worker pools running heterogeneous contexts (512 & 2048) and emit steady 200 RPS load with occasional bursts to 600 RPS
3) On a Private VPC stack replicate customer config (kv_cache enabled, prefetch=on, kernel_selection=auto), run the sample prompt set from Confluence and measure TTFT and tokens/sec over 15 minutes
4) Observe first-byte latency spikes, divergence between kernel variants, and tokens/sec drop that correlates with prefetch saturation events.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 22:05 UTC: Pager alert from Datadog - first_byte_latency P95 increased by 3x in us-west-2 for hosted API; customers AcmeHealth and Finova opened escalations

2026-03-09 22:22 UTC: Initial triage identified recent kernel-selection heuristic change in commit 9c4f21 which biases 'preferred_kernel' for long-contexts; hypothesis: suboptimal kernel leads to lower microbatch throughput and longer priming time

2026-03-09 23:10 UTC: Replayed traffic against canary runtime with heuristic revert; P50 TTFT recovered but some workloads still show tokens/sec drop under sustained fanout—investigation points to an interaction between kv-prefetch queue saturation and the new scheduler throttling policy

2026-03-10 02:00 UTC: Memory and KV eviction traces show bursty prefetch requests causing head-of-line blocking in the coalescer; throttling policy defers microbatch aggregation leading to smaller batch sizes and per-token cost increase

Root cause summary: combined effect of kernel-selection heuristic + aggressive kv-prefetch behavior + scheduler backpressure. This triad causes bifurcation: some requests pick the slow kernel path and experience TTFT spikes, while others suffer throughput collapse due to reduced batching.
mitigations: Short-term (hotpatch): roll back kernel-selection heuristic (revert commit 9c4f21) and introduce a conservative cap on concurrent prefetches per-worker to 6
Introduce a prefetch circuit-breaker that drops non-critical prefetches when coalescer queue depth > 75%
Apply regional routing steering to shift bursty traffic to secondary pools for 24 hours while we monitor
Medium-term: implement scheduler metric to track effective microbatch size and automatic fallback to 'stable' kernel when batching drops below threshold
Long-term: add model-aware kernel benchmarking and an on-deploy calibration phase that prevents heuristic flips without controlled A/B validation.
actions: A) Prepare hotpatch branch: revert/emit conservative prefetch cap (owner: Rafael) - PR ready
B) Run canary in us-west-2 with steady-state and burst profiles for 4 hours (owner: SRE: Lina Cho)
C) Notify impacted customers with interim mitigation steps and ETA for fix (owner: CS: Miguel Ortiz)
D) After canary success, promote hotpatch to hosted and Dedicated pools; schedule out-of-band patch for Private customers with upgrade notes
E) Postmortem and follow-up epic for scheduler/kernels redesign (owner: Research/Runtime)
notes: Customer comms: AcmeHealth notified 2026-03-09 23:30 UTC — committed to temporary routing and ETA 12 hours for canary validation
Finova escalation requires an SLO credit assessment if windows persist beyond 48 hours
SRE runbook updated with 'prefetch circuit-breaker' toggle and emergency rollback steps
Design/PM asked to prioritize a UX control for per-model kernel pinning in Console to reduce blast radius of automatic heuristic changes
deployment_plan: 1) Merge hotpatch PR to release branch; 2) Canary deploy to us-west-2 hosted pool (25% traffic) + Dedicated small pool; 3) Run synthetic and customer-config replays for 4 hours; 4) If metrics OK (TTFT P95 within 1.2x baseline, tokens/sec >= 95% baseline) promote to remaining regions and schedule Private rollout via customer-upgrade packages.
rollback_plan: If canary shows regressions revert to previous commit via automated rollback job and re-enable previous prefetch thresholds. Notify customers that we have restored prior behavior and open follow-up ticket to re-evaluate heuristic with controlled experiment.
